Frequently asked questions

My buyer pulled out. Can I make them pay my costs?

Almost never. In England and Wales neither side is committed until exchange of contracts. Before that point a buyer can walk away without giving a reason, without notice, and without owing you anything, including your solicitor's abortive fees. The one exception is a reservation agreement, where the buyer put down a deposit of roughly £500 to £1,000 when the offer was agreed. If you had one and they pulled out without good reason, you keep that deposit. Ask your solicitor whether anything you signed covers it.

How common is it for a sale to fall through?

Common enough that it isn't a reflection on you or your house. Q1 2026 figures from Quick Move Now put the UK fall-through rate at about 22.5%. OnTheMarket and Reeds Rains put it nearer 25.8% for the same period. That is roughly one in four agreed sales collapsing before exchange. Survey problems drove 37.5% of them, the single biggest cause. These figures move every quarter, so check the latest published data if you need a current number.

What has the collapsed sale actually cost me?

It depends how far things had got. Your solicitor charges for the work they did, so an abortive file usually runs between £500 and £1,000 once searches and enquiries were under way, and a good deal less if it fell over early. An EPC costs £60 to £120 and stays valid for ten years, so it carries straight into your next sale. If your agent works on a no sale, no fee basis you owe them nothing, but check what you signed. The buyer's survey was their cost, not yours. Ask your solicitor for a written breakdown.

Should I relist with the same agent or switch?

Look at how they handled the buyer before you decide. A good agent will have checked the buyer's mortgage agreement in principle and their position in the chain before recommending you accept. If that didn't happen, the same thing can happen again. Relisting with the same agent costs you nothing and is quickest to arrange. Switching means reading your contract first, because sole agency agreements usually have a tie-in and a notice period. Either way, ask the next agent to prove the buyer's funding before you take the house off the market.

The buyer hasn't pulled out, they have just gone quiet. What should I do?

Treat silence as a warning, not a delay. The signs of a sale in real trouble are a buyer who has stopped answering their own solicitor, searches that have expired with nobody agreeing to refresh them, a mortgage offer that has lapsed with no update, or their own sale collapsing without them confirming they still want to go ahead. Ask your solicitor to write formally, requesting written confirmation that the buyer intends to proceed, with a clear deadline. If the deadline passes with no reply, you can treat the sale as withdrawn and move on.

Does going back on the market make my house look damaged?

A little, and it is worth being honest about it. Buyers and agents can see how long a property has been listed and whether the price has moved. A second listing invites the question of what the survey found. You can get ahead of it by having the issue quoted or fixed, and by telling the next buyer up front. If the property has been listed twice already, or the problem is one a lender won't accept, a sale that doesn't depend on a mortgage removes the question entirely.

You don't need to read the rest. Send us the property details and we'll come back the same day with a written offer, valid for 14 days.

Get my free cash offer

The survey killed the sale. Will that just happen again?

With another mortgaged buyer, quite possibly. Survey problems drove 37.5% of Q1 2026 fall-throughs, and the same report will come back on the next survey unless the work is done. Damp, structural movement, subsidence, knotweed and non-standard construction are the usual culprits, and lenders react to them, not just buyers. We don't rely on a mortgage survey, so condition doesn't put our purchase at risk. We look at the property, price it as it stands, and buy it that way.

How quickly can you complete if my chain has just collapsed?

We complete in 7 to 28 days once we have agreed a price, and the fastest we have done is 7 days. There is no mortgage lender, no survey down-valuation and no onward purchase behind us, so the things that usually break a sale aren't in the way. If you need longer, because you are still finding somewhere to move to, we work to your date instead.

Can you buy if I am also buying somewhere else?

Yes, and this is one of the more common reasons people call us. We buy your property and you become a chain free buyer on the place you want, which is a much stronger position to negotiate from. We can also complete and let you stay on for an agreed period while you finish your own purchase. Tell us the date you are working to and we will fit around it rather than the other way round.

Am I still tied to my estate agent?

Possibly, so read the agreement before you agree anything with us. Most sole agency contracts have a tie-in period, a notice period, and a clause about buyers they introduced. Ask the agent in writing when you are free to sell elsewhere. Once that is clear, we can put a written offer to you the same day, valid for 14 days.

Isn't a cash buyer just an auction by another name?

No, they work quite differently. At auction you pay entry and commission fees, the price isn't known until the day, and completion is normally fixed at 28 days whether that suits you or not. With us the figure is agreed in writing before you commit, there are no fees taken off it, and you choose the completion date. Auction can beat us on price when a property attracts competing bidders. It is worth comparing both rather than assuming.

Do I have to tell you why the last sale fell through?

It helps, and nothing you say will put us off. If a survey turned something up, showing us the report often speeds things up, because it answers questions we would otherwise ask. If the buyer simply changed their mind, that tells us the property is fine and the buyer wasn't. Either way we would rather know at the start than find it during conveyancing, and we would rather give you an honest answer up front than an offer we later have to move.

Question we haven't answered?

Put it on the form with your property details and we'll answer it straight, even if the answer is that a cash sale isn't right for you.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell my house without it being listed online?

Yes. We buy directly with our own funds, so the property never goes on Rightmove, Zoopla or any other portal. There is no listing to find and nothing for anyone to search.

Will there be a For Sale board outside my house?

No. We never put a board up. There is nothing outside the property at any point, before or after the sale.

Do I have to let strangers view the house?

No. There are no open-market viewings and nobody from the public comes round. One of our team will usually want to see the property once, at a time that suits you. That is the only visit.

Will my neighbours find out what I sold for?

Eventually, yes, and no buyer can honestly promise otherwise. Sold prices are recorded by HM Land Registry and published on their Price Paid data, usually two to six months after completion. What a discreet sale avoids is the months of visible activity beforehand: the board, the listing, the viewings and the questions. It doesn't erase the public record afterwards.

Can I sell discreetly if I still have a mortgage?

Yes. Your lender has to be told, because the mortgage is redeemed out of the sale proceeds on completion. That is a normal part of any sale and is handled between the solicitors. It doesn't make the sale public.

Is a discreet sale confidential from my family or my partner?

Not always, and we won't pretend otherwise. If the property is jointly owned, every owner has to agree and sign. If you are the sole owner, the decision is yours. In a divorce or separation you may also have a legal duty to disclose the sale. Take your own advice on that.

Do you need identification and paperwork?

Yes. Anti-money-laundering rules require the solicitors to verify your identity and the source of funds. That is a legal requirement on any property sale in the UK. Those checks are private and go no further than the firms involved.

Is a discreet sale always the right choice?

The right route depends on the property, the written terms and your priorities. Compare fees, ongoing bills, buyer funding and the proposed completion date. We assess each property individually and explain our offer without an obligation to accept.

How quickly can a discreet sale complete?

Typically 7 to 28 days from you accepting the offer, on a date you choose. There is no chain and no buyer's mortgage to wait for.

One of us still needs to see it once before completion, at a time that suits you. The figure can move if the condition turns out different. But you get a real number first.

If I get in touch, will I start getting calls from loads of other companies?

No, not from us. We don't sell your details and we don't pass them to estate agents, brokers or lead sites. So you shouldn't start getting cold calls out of the blue. Your enquiry is seen by our own team, the system we use to manage enquiries, and later the solicitors doing the sale. Our privacy policy sets out exactly who your data goes to. If you would rather we didn't leave a voicemail, or you want us to ring at a set time, just say.

How much would I actually walk away with?

We assess each property individually, taking account of its condition, location, tenure and the information you share. We explain our offer and its conditions in writing. There is no obligation to accept, and you can ask your solicitor to review the terms.

If I say yes and then change my mind, am I stuck with it?

No. Accepting an offer isn't legally binding until contracts are exchanged. You can walk away before then and you won't owe us anything. Our offer stays open for 14 days, so you have time to think it over or get advice without being chased. We would far rather you pulled out early than went through with something that wasn't right for you.

There is a court date coming up. Is it too late to sell quietly?

Often it isn't too late, but it depends how far things have gone. If a hearing is booked, a sale that is genuinely moving can sometimes be put to your lender or the court. They may agree to hold off. That decision is theirs, not ours. Ring us with the dates and we will tell you straight whether we can move fast enough. Shelter and StepChange give free advice on this too.

How soon would I have to be out of the house?

You choose the completion date, so that is up to you. Some people want it done in a week. Others need a month or more to sort somewhere to live. We can work to a fixed date if you have one. You do need to be out by completion day, because that is when the house stops being yours. If your plans slip, tell us early and we can usually move it.

Do I have to pay anything up front?

Nothing up front, and no fees to us at any stage. No valuation fee, no admin fee, no commission. We can cover your legal fees if you use our panel solicitor. You can use your own solicitor instead, which is your right, but you would then pay their bill yourself. Anything still owed on the mortgage comes out of the sale money at completion, and the solicitors handle it.

When you come round, will anyone be able to tell who you are?

No. One of us turns up in an ordinary car with no signage, no branding and nothing to hand out. Usually one person, usually under an hour. If you would rather we came at a quiet time, or parked further down the road, just tell us and we will. To anyone looking out of a window it is a visitor, because that is all it is.

Put it on the form with your property details and we'll answer it straight, even if the answer is that a cash sale isn't right for you.

Which situation are you in?

A. Amicable joint sale

Both of you want the house sold and the money split. The simplest case, and the most common one.

B. Contested sale

One of you wants to sell. The other won't engage or won't sign the TR1. That route runs through the family court.

C. Buy-out

One of you keeps the house and remortgages to pay the other their share. It turns on what a lender will accept.

D. After the final order

The final order is in place and a consent order requires a sale by a date or a trigger event.

E. Before the settlement

The divorce has started but the money isn't settled. You can still sell. The proceeds usually wait in the solicitor's account.

F. You weren't married

TOLATA 1996 applies rather than the Matrimonial Causes Act. There is no such thing as common-law marriage here.

The legal framework in 2026, what has changed

Two laws matter here. The Matrimonial Causes Act 1973 still governs the money side of a marriage ending. Sections 23, 24, 24A and 25 give the court its powers: lump sums, transferring the house, forcing a sale, and deciding a fair split. The judge weighs up what each of you needs, what each of you put in, and above all the welfare of any child under 18. The Divorce, Dissolution and Separation Act 2020 changed the divorce process itself in April 2022 and brought in no-fault divorce. It set two waits you can't get round: 20 weeks from the application to the conditional order, then another 6 weeks to the final order.

The case to know is Standish v Standish [2025] UKSC 26. The Supreme Court used it to set out what counts as shared marital property, what stays with one person, and how each is split. Any advice that ignores it is out of date.

The latest ONS data on divorces in England and Wales show that most divorces now go through with no blame attached to either side. The whole thing usually takes well over a year. So most couples have to decide what to do about the house during the divorce, not after it.

The four practical routes to selling the family home

Sell on the open market

Usually the most money and the longest wait. About 5 to 6 months here, agent fees near 1.4% including VAT, and a chain that can still break.

Buy one another out

One of you keeps the house and remortgages for the other's share, with a TR1 to transfer the title. It fails when a lender won't lend on one income.

Ask the court to order a sale

Where one of you won't engage, the other can apply under section 24A MCA 1973, or section 14 TOLATA if you weren't married.

Best if you both want it finished

Can my ex stop the sale? Can the court force one?

If you own the house jointly, you both have to agree to sell. Without a court order, neither of you can make the other sign the TR1. If only your husband or wife is on the deeds, you still have home rights under Part IV of the Family Law Act 1996. Your solicitor registers a Class F land charge against the title, and that stops the house being sold over your head.

But the corollary is also true: the court can force the sale. Either spouse can apply under section 24A MCA 1973 as part of financial remedy proceedings. Cohabiting co-owners apply under section 14 TOLATA 1996. It isn't a quick fix. Most South Yorkshire money hearings are listed at Sheffield Combined Court Centre, and a fought case can take 12 to 18 months. But the route exists, and just knowing that is often enough to bring a reluctant ex back to the table.

Capital Gains Tax, the mortgage, and pensions

Three financial points trip up most divorcing couples on the property side.

Capital Gains Tax. You have three years to move the house between you without a tax bill. The clock starts at the end of the tax year you separated in, under rules that changed on 6 April 2023. There's no time limit at all where the transfer is made under a court order or a formal divorce agreement. Most sales of a main home are covered by Private Residence Relief anyway. Gov.uk has the official guidance. If you separated late in a tax year, or you're outside the three years, get tax advice on your own dates.

The mortgage. Whichever route you take, the mortgage is paid off in full on completion, and you are both released from it once that clears. Watch for an Early Repayment Charge if you are part-way through a fixed deal. It's usually 1% to 5% of what you still owe, so it can run to thousands. Your mortgage offer will say, or ring your lender and ask.

Pensions. Property and pensions are usually balanced against each other in the financial settlement. One party keeping more of the housing equity often means the other taking a larger share of the pension. Don't settle the house without looking at the pension. Getting that wrong is what divorced people most often regret, in the University of Bristol's Fair Shares research. It also found most couples never get a consent order at all, which leaves the money side open for years afterwards. Get one.

Selling a house during divorce in South Yorkshire, the local picture

If you're in Sheffield, Doncaster, Rotherham or Barnsley, three things matter: which court hears your case, what your house is worth, and which local solicitor to ring. Here they are.

The family courts

Sheffield Combined Court Centre houses the Designated Family Court for South Yorkshire: Law Courts, 50 West Bar, Sheffield S3 8PH (switchboard 0114 281 2400). It hears financial-remedy applications affecting Sheffield, Rotherham and, increasingly, Doncaster cases.

Doncaster Justice Centre North on College Road is permanently closed. Unsafe concrete (RAAC) was found in the building. Doncaster family hearings have moved to Doncaster Justice Centre South, Sheffield Magistrates' Court, Sheffield Combined Court Centre and Barnsley Law Court, or are held remotely on the Cloud Video Platform. Read your listing letter carefully. Your hearing may not be where you expect.

Barnsley Law Court takes overflow family work from Doncaster and Sheffield in addition to its own caseload.

What homes are worth locally (Land Registry)

The average home costs around £222,000 in Sheffield, £191,000 in Rotherham, £174,000 in Barnsley and £170,000 in Doncaster. Prices have edged up in all four over the past year. Where houses are cheaper, a buy-out is easier for one of you to fund, but there is less to split at the end. You can look up what houses on your own street actually sold for, free, on the Land Registry website.

Mediation and Resolution-accredited solicitors

Before you can go to court about money, you have to attend a MIAM (a Mandatory Information Assessment Meeting) with an accredited mediator. Ask about the Family Mediation Voucher Scheme when you book, which has given families up to £500 towards the cost. Mediators near Sheffield include MESH Mediation, Family Mediation Yorkshire (based in Barnsley, covering Sheffield and Rotherham) and Family Matters Mediation (Rotherham and Sheffield).

For legal advice, Resolution's Find a Member directory lists South Yorkshire family solicitors who have signed up to work constructively rather than pick fights. Sheffield family teams include Irwin Mitchell, Wake Smith, Switalskis, Keebles, Banner Jones and Howells; Sills & Betteridge cover Doncaster; Wilford Smith and Howells cover Rotherham; Howells covers Barnsley. Confirm individual accreditation via the Resolution postcode search before instructing.

Get Your Free Cash Offer

Common scams, and how to verify a legitimate cash buyer

Nobody regulates cash house buyers directly. The nearest thing is The Property Ombudsman's code for property buying companies, the National Association of Property Buyers, and ordinary consumer law. That leaves divorcing sellers exposed, because you are under time pressure, worn down, and often not being told everything. Run these six checks before you sign anything. Each takes minutes, and either of you can do them alone.

Companies House. Search the buyer's legal company name and number on Companies House. Look for active status, filed accounts, a real registered office, and named directors.

Proof of funds. Ask for a PDF bank statement (not a screenshot) on a named business account, dated within 14 days, showing cleared funds. Or a solicitor's letter on letterhead confirming cleared funds in client account.

TPO and NAPB membership. Verify on the live TPO member directory. If a buyer claims membership but isn't listed, the claim is false.

Reviews with detail. Look for reviews left steadily over the past year that describe a real sale. Read the one-star ones. What people complain about tells you more than the star average.

Footer signals. The website should display company number, registered office, ICO registration, and complaints procedure link. Missing signals are signals.

Your own solicitor. Each spouse instructs their own. A single solicitor can't act for both parties in a divorce sale, there is an inherent conflict of interest. Verify any solicitor's authorisation on the Law Society's Find a Solicitor register.

A legitimate buyer welcomes all six checks. A buyer who pushes back on any of them is telling you something useful.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell the family home during a divorce without my spouse's agreement?

Not on your own, no. If you own it jointly, you both have to agree. If you can't agree, either of you can ask the court to order the sale under section 24A of the Matrimonial Causes Act 1973 if you are married or in a civil partnership, or section 14 of the Trusts of Land and Appointment of Trustees Act 1996 if you lived together but didn't marry. Courts don't order a sale lightly. The welfare of any child under 18 comes first.

What is a Mesher order, and when does the court use one?

A Mesher order puts the sale off until a set trigger: usually the youngest child turning 18, the parent living there remarrying or moving a partner in, or a fixed date. Courts use it when there isn't enough equity to house you both separately right now. The downside is real. The one who moves out has their money locked in the house for years.

What is a Martin order?

A Martin order gives one spouse the right to occupy the home for life (or until they remarry or cohabit), at which point the property is sold and the proceeds split. It is rarer than a Mesher order and used where the asset pool is large enough to support indefinite occupation by one party.

Can we sell the house before the divorce is finalised?

Yes. A sale can legally complete at any point. In practice your solicitors will want the money held in a client account until the financial order is made, so neither of you can be accused of spending assets before the settlement is agreed.

How does Capital Gains Tax work on the matrimonial home during divorce?

You have three years to move the house between you without a Capital Gains Tax bill. The clock starts at the end of the tax year you separated in, under rules that changed on 6 April 2023. There is no time limit where the transfer is made under a court order or a formal divorce agreement. Most sales of a main home are covered by Private Residence Relief anyway. Check your own dates with a tax adviser.

What happens to the mortgage when we sell?

The mortgage is paid off in full out of the sale money on the day you complete. You are both released from it once that payment clears. If you are part-way through a fixed deal there may be an Early Repayment Charge, usually 1% to 5% of what you still owe. Check your mortgage offer, or ring your lender and ask.

Who gets the money from the sale in a divorce?

Not automatically 50/50. It depends on the financial settlement. The court weighs up the section 25 Matrimonial Causes Act 1973 factors: what each of you needs, sharing, compensation, the welfare of any child under 18, what each of you contributed, how long you were married, and what each of you can earn. Most couples agree it by consent order without ever going to a hearing.

Do I have to sign the TR1? What if my ex refuses?

A TR1 is the Land Registry form that transfers legal title at completion. Both registered owners must sign for a sale to complete. If your ex refuses, either party can apply to court under section 24A MCA 1973 or section 14 TOLATA 1996 for an order requiring sale. Family courts can also order that the recalcitrant party's signature be dispensed with where necessary.

Can my cohabiting partner force a sale? (We're not married.)

Yes, either of you can apply, but the rules are different when you aren't married. There is no automatic right to a share of the other person's assets in England and Wales. Common-law marriage is a myth. A dispute over a jointly owned home is decided under the Trusts of Land and Appointment of Trustees Act 1996, by whose name is on the title at the Land Registry and any declaration of trust. Either co-owner can apply for a sale under section 14 TOLATA.

How quickly can a cash sale complete during divorce proceedings?

South Yorkshire Property Buyers can complete in as little as 7 days, with most divorce-related sales completing in 7 to 28 days once both parties' solicitors are instructed. An estate agent route typically takes 5-6 months from listing to completion.

What does a cash buyer typically pay?

We assess each property individually, using its condition, location, tenure and the information you give us. We explain our offer in writing so you can consider it without obligation. It may change if legal checks reveal a material issue or the property differs from its description.

Can I use my own solicitor instead of yours?

Yes, always. You can instruct any SRA-regulated solicitor you like. In a divorce sale you each need your own family solicitor anyway, because one solicitor can't act for both of you. We can cover your legal fees if you use our panel solicitor, but you are free to use your own and pay for it yourself.

What if there is negative equity?

If you owe more than the house will sell for, that shortfall has to be dealt with before your lender will release its charge and let the sale go through. You can try to agree terms with the lender, split the shortfall between you as part of the settlement, or wait and hope prices recover. Get advice from your solicitor and from the free services at MoneyHelper or StepChange.

How do I check that a cash buyer is legitimate?

Run six checks. Look the company up on Companies House. Ask for a recent dated PDF proof of funds from a named business account. Check they are listed by The Property Ombudsman and the National Association of Property Buyers. Read the reviews, including the bad ones. Check the website footer shows a company number and registered office. And instruct your own solicitor, not theirs.

How the SYPB process works

All your options for selling quickly compared

This page is a general guide and not legal, tax or financial advice. Every divorce is different. Before making decisions about the matrimonial home, take advice from a Resolution-accredited family-law solicitor, an FMC-accredited mediator, or the free services at Citizens Advice and MoneyHelper.

Do I have to move out of the house while we sort the divorce out?

No. Being married gives you the right to stay in the family home, even if the deeds are only in your husband's or wife's name. Neither of you can force the other out without a court order. If you feel unsafe, speak to a family solicitor about an occupation order straight away, or ring the police if you are in danger. Moving out for some peace doesn't mean you give up your share of the money.

The house is only in my husband's name. Can he sell it without telling me?

Not easily, if you protect your position now. Because you are married you have what the law calls home rights, and your solicitor can register a notice against the property at the Land Registry. That notice shows up on any sale or remortgage, so a buyer or lender sees it and the sale stalls. Do this as early as you can. If you aren't married, the rules are different, so get advice quickly.

My ex has stopped paying the mortgage. What happens to me?

You are still on the hook. If the mortgage is in both names you are each responsible for all of it, not half each, and missed payments hit both credit files. The lender can chase either of you for the full amount. Tell them you have separated, because many will agree a short-term arrangement, and pay what you can. If the mortgage is in your ex's sole name only they are liable, but the arrears still come out of what you both walk away with.

Do we actually have to sell the house, or is there another way?

No, selling isn't the only option. One of you may be able to buy the other out by taking the mortgage on alone, if a lender will accept you on your income by yourself. Where there are children, a court can put the sale off until they are older. Selling is often the cleanest way to free up the money and untangle your finances. A family solicitor can tell you which options your actual figures will support.

We can't agree what the house is worth. How do we sort that out?

Get more than one opinion in writing. Three local estate agent valuations are the usual starting point, and if you still can't agree you can jointly pay for a RICS surveyor to value it properly, which a court will take seriously. Sold prices for homes near you are free to look up on the Land Registry website. If you ask us for an offer, you get it in writing the same day, and both of you get the same figure on the same terms.

Can we sell without the whole street finding out?

We can keep it quiet, but we can't promise total secrecy. Selling to us means no For Sale board, no online listing and no stream of strangers walking round your home. We usually only need one visit, and we don't discuss your situation with anyone outside the sale. What we can't control is the public record, because once the sale completes the price is registered with the Land Registry and turns up on property websites later.

Would we get more money if we just waited and used an estate agent?

The right route depends on the property, the written terms and your priorities. Compare fees, ongoing bills, buyer funding and the proposed completion date. We assess each property individually and explain our offer without an obligation to accept.

Who pays for all this? We can barely afford the solicitors as it is.

You pay no estate agent fees and nothing to us, and we can cover your legal fees on the sale if you use our panel solicitor. You will each still need your own solicitor for the divorce itself, and that bill is separate. Sale costs normally come out of the completion money rather than your pocket today. Ask for every figure in writing before you agree to anything, from us or from anybody else.

My ex won't let anyone in the house. Can you still buy it?

Usually yes, but we do need to see inside at some point. We normally only need one short visit, and we can arrange it for a time when just one of you is home if that is easier. If your ex refuses access completely, your solicitors will need to deal with it, because we can't buy a house we have never been inside. Tell us early and we will work around it as best we can.

If we accept your offer and then change our minds, are we stuck?

No. Our offer is free and comes with no obligation, so you aren't tied in and there is no penalty for pulling out, right up until contracts are exchanged. Our written offer stays open for 14 days, so you both have time to take it to your own solicitors. Divorce sales do fall through when people change their minds, and we would far rather you were sure. If things change later, tell us and we can pick it up again when you are ready.

Can I just sell my half to you and be done with it?

In almost all cases, no. We buy whole houses rather than one person's share, because a half share is very hard to sell on and the mortgage stays in both names anyway. What we can do is give you both the same written offer for the whole property, so each of you can take identical figures to your own solicitor. If you want out and your ex wants to stay, a buy-out is normally the route.

What probate means for a property sale

Probate is the legal process that sorts out a dead person's affairs so what's left can pass to those who inherit. If there is a house, it can't legally change hands until the right authority is in place. The person in charge is the executor named in the will. If there is no will, the court appoints an administrator under the intestacy rules. In law both are called personal representatives.

The document that unlocks the sale is the Grant of Probate, or the Grant of Letters of Administration where there is no will. It comes from His Majesty's Courts and Tribunals Service through the online probate application. It proves you have the legal authority to deal with the estate. Without it, the property's title can't be transferred. You can exchange contracts before it arrives if the buyer is willing to wait. Completion has to come after the Grant, never before.

So there are two clocks running. One you control: when to market the house, accept an offer and instruct solicitors. One you don't: probate itself, plus any HMRC and lender steps. Most probate sales that go wrong go wrong because nobody separated the two at the start.

How long probate actually takes in 2026

Most online probate applications now reach the Grant in about 2 to 5 weeks. Older guides say 16 weeks, or even 6 months. That was true during the HMCTS backlog of 2023 and early 2024, but it's out of date. The latest Family Court Statistics Quarterly shows the shorter times. Paper applications take longer, and so do cases the court stops to query something.

Sorting the whole estate still takes roughly 6 to 12 months, because the Grant is only one step. You also have to value the estate, do the Inheritance Tax forms, pay any tax due, show the Grant to the banks and other asset holders, sell the property and close the accounts.

What you can, and can't, do before the Grant is issued

You can market it

Put it up for sale, hold viewings and accept an offer. None of that needs the Grant.

You can get it valued

You have to, for HMRC. A RICS surveyor or an estate agent can do it before the Grant.

You can exchange contracts

Exchange subject to Grant, so long as the buyer accepts that completion waits for the paperwork.

You can't complete

Legal title can't be transferred until the Grant is in place. Anyone who tells you otherwise is wrong.

A mortgage offer can run out

A buyer's offer usually lasts 3 to 6 months. If the Grant takes longer than that, the sale can fail.

A cash sale has nothing to expire

No lender and no offer running down, so we can exchange now and complete when the Grant lands.

A word on the auction figure, because it's the easiest one to misread. With the modern method of auction, the buyer pays a non-refundable reservation fee on top of the hammer price, usually around 5% plus VAT. It's described as the buyer's fee, not the seller's. But a buyer works to a total budget, so that fee comes out of what they can bid and pushes the hammer price down by roughly the same amount. The estate's own auction fees then come off that lower figure. The point isn't that we always leave the estate with more. It's that a hammer price and a cash offer aren't the same thing, so compare what actually lands in the estate's account.

Inheritance Tax, Capital Gains Tax, and the "probate value"

There are two tax conversations to have, and they apply at different points.

Inheritance Tax (IHT) is worked out on the whole estate as it stood on the date of death. Each person has a nil-rate band of £325,000, frozen until at least April 2031. If a main home passes to children or grandchildren, a residence nil-rate band of £175,000 can be added, taking the threshold to £500,000 each. Bands pass between spouses, so a widowed estate can often shelter up to £1 million before any IHT is due. Above the threshold the rate is 40%. Where IHT is payable, it has to be paid before the Grant is issued, usually straight from the deceased's bank account through the HMRC Direct Payment Scheme.

Capital Gains Tax (CGT) is worked out on the gain between the probate value (the figure on the IHT forms) and the price the house actually sells for. Executors get £3,000 a year tax free. Above that, a house is taxed at 18% or 24%, depending on the tax band. Sell at or near the probate value and there is little or no CGT. Leave it for years in a rising market and the bill builds up.

If the property sells for less than probate value: the executor can claim IHT loss relief on form IHT38 within 4 years, reducing the IHT bill retrospectively. This is widely overlooked.

If the estate is comfortably under the threshold, the IHT side is just paperwork. Declare it and move on. If it's near the threshold, or there is more than one property, the way probate value, IHT and CGT work together can decide which sale route is right. That is worth paying a probate solicitor or a STEP-qualified tax adviser to look at.

What should executors check before accepting a cash offer?

Yes, a beneficiary can question any decision you make as executor. But the law is clear about what you owe them, and a cash sale you can explain and evidence meets that duty. This is the worry we hear most often from executors, so it's worth setting out properly.

The leading case is Buttle v Saunders [1950] 2 All ER 193. It says personal representatives must get the best price reasonably obtainable. The important word is "reasonably". You don't have to chase the highest possible number whatever the cost, risk or delay. You have to make a sensible commercial decision for the estate, and be able to show why.

One more point, on what you have to tell a buyer. Since Patarkatsishvili v Woodward-Fisher [2025], the courts have made clear that sellers can be held liable for hiding known problems on the TA6 property information form. If the deceased knew about damp, knotweed, structural trouble or an ongoing dispute, say so. Being straight about it protects the estate from claims later. It doesn't affect our offer either way.

Selling a probate property across South Yorkshire, what differs by borough

Empty-home rules are set by each council, not nationally, which is why national probate guides only get you so far. Here is how the four South Yorkshire boroughs we cover most differ.

Sheffield

Probate houses here tend to be terraces in S5, S6 and S35, ex-council semis, and long-held detached homes in Dore, Totley and Fulwood. Sheffield City Council charges a 100% empty-homes council tax premium once a house has been empty 12 months. Conservation area rules can slow renovation down in S7, S10 and S11.

Doncaster

Doncaster has a flood history that matters here. Bentley, Toll Bar and Fishlake were badly hit in 2007 and 2019. Houses in those areas often need specialist insurance that costs thousands a year, and they can be hard to get a mortgage on, which shrinks the pool of buyers. The empty-homes premium starts at 12 months.

Rotherham

Rotherham put off its 12-month empty-homes premium until April 2026. It's live now, so the clock starts later than Sheffield's, but waiting no longer pays. The old industrial suburbs and former mining villages have more houses needing modernising.

Barnsley

Houses needing serious renovation are the main type of probate sale here. Terraces in the centre and the former mining communities are some of the cheapest stock in South Yorkshire. Barnsley Council charges the 12-month empty-homes premium. It has also been more active than most boroughs in chasing run-down properties through enforcement.

We also buy in Chesterfield (Derbyshire), Worksop and Retford (Bassetlaw), Mansfield (Nottinghamshire) and Gainsborough (West Lindsey). Different councils, different empty-home rules, same approach.

We are a small local team. We buy with our own funds, and the person who answers the phone is the person who decides. The family sets the pace, not us.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell a probate house before the Grant is issued?

You can market it, accept an offer and even exchange contracts before the Grant, as long as the buyer accepts that completion waits for it. What you can't do is transfer the title before the Grant arrives. A cash buyer willing to exchange subject to Grant gives you certainty without forcing a timeline you can't control.

How long does probate take in 2026?

Usually 2 to 5 weeks for a clean online application with no Inheritance Tax complications. Paper applications take longer, and so do cases the court stops to query something. Sorting the whole estate, from death to final distribution, still takes about 6 to 12 months. That is the other steps, not the Grant.

Do all executors have to agree to the sale?

Yes, if you have all taken out the Grant. Executors who have taken out the Grant must agree unanimously on the big decisions, including selling the house. If one has had power reserved, or has formally renounced, the rest can act without them. A real deadlock can go to court, but most disagreements settle once everyone sees the same clearly written offer.

What happens if the will is contested?

A caveat lodged with the Probate Registry by someone disputing the will stops the Grant being issued. Until that is resolved, the sale can't complete. We can still look at the property and put an offer in writing, but we wouldn't exchange contracts while a caveat is live. Contested probates are more common than they used to be.

Do I need a RICS valuation, or will an estate agent valuation do?

An estate agent valuation is usually fine if the estate is well under the Inheritance Tax threshold. If it's close to or above the threshold, HMRC much prefers a RICS Red Book valuation, because it follows a set method and is harder to challenge later. If you aren't sure, especially on a higher-value house, take the RICS valuation.

Will the estate pay Inheritance Tax?

It depends on what the whole estate is worth. The nil-rate band is £325,000 per person, plus up to £175,000 more if the main home passes to children or grandchildren. Bands pass between spouses, so a widowed estate can often shelter up to £1 million. Above the threshold, IHT is charged at 40% on the excess, and some reliefs can apply. For an answer about your estate, ring the HMRC Inheritance Tax helpline or speak to a probate solicitor.

Is there Capital Gains Tax when an executor sells a probate house?

CGT applies to the gain between the probate value and the price the house sells for. Executors get £3,000 a year tax free. Above that, a house is taxed at 18% or 24%. Sell close to the probate value and there is little CGT to pay. Leave it and sell into a rising market and the bill builds. If the house sells for less than the probate value, you can claim IHT38 loss relief within 4 years.

What if the property is in poor condition or in negative equity?

Neither is a problem for us. We buy in any condition: empty for years, needing a full renovation, with title quirks, with knotweed, with subsidence, with a mortgage still outstanding. If the house is in negative equity, meaning the mortgage is bigger than the sale will raise, there are set steps to follow with the lender. We have dealt with those before and can talk you through them.

How does the empty-homes council tax premium affect us?

A probate property gets up to 12 months free of council tax after the Grant. That is the Class I exception, and it means the clock that matters starts at the Grant, not when the house became empty. After that, councils can charge a 100% premium, which is double council tax, on a house empty for 12 months or more. Sheffield, Doncaster and Barnsley apply it at the 12-month mark. Rotherham started in April 2026.

What should executors consider before accepting a cash offer?

If you are selling for an estate or on someone else’s behalf, ask your solicitor what authority and evidence you need before accepting an offer. Keep valuations, written terms and a record of the options considered. We can discuss the property while you obtain that advice, without an obligation to proceed.

Will a cash sale fall through if probate takes longer than expected?

Not with us. We have no mortgage and no lender's surveyor, so there is no offer expiry on our side. Once we agree a price we hold it while you wait. We will exchange whenever you are ready, and complete on the Grant date itself if that suits. A long wait for the Grant doesn't change our figure on its own. The one thing that could is the legal work turning up something material, such as a title or structural problem. We would put any change in writing and explain it.

How can we verify any cash buyer, including you, before committing?

A few quick checks cover the main risks. Look the company up on Companies House. Ask for proof of funds. A solicitor's letter on letterhead confirming cleared funds is worth far more than a screenshot. Read the company's reviews. Check they belong to a redress scheme, such as The Property Ombudsman. Ask your probate solicitor for an independent view. They have a duty to the estate, not to us. We will support every one of those checks.

Mum has died and there's no will. Can we still sell her house?

Yes. Without a will you apply for Letters of Administration instead of a Grant of Probate, and the closest relative is usually the one who applies. Who inherits is then set by law rather than by a will. Once that document arrives, the sale completes in exactly the same way. We can look at the house and put an offer in writing while you wait for it.

Who pays the council tax and the bills while the house sits empty?

The estate pays them, and sorting it out falls to you as executor. The urgent one is insurance. Most policies change or lapse once a house is empty, so tell the insurer straight away and ask about unoccupied cover. Council tax can be free for a set period, and your council will confirm how long. After that it starts, and it can later double. Utilities, gardening and security carry on too.

Do we have to empty the house of all his things before you buy it?

No. We buy the property, not what is inside it. Take the time you need with belongings, and if there are things you can't face sorting, tell us and we will agree in writing what stays. Some families clear everything, some leave nearly all of it. We will talk it through and set the arrangement before completion, and we won't rush you through the sorting out.

My aunt is still living in the house. Can it be sold?

Not with us until her position is sorted out, and that has to happen before contracts are exchanged. Sometimes a person living there has a right to stay and sometimes they don't, and only your solicitor can tell you which. We won't buy over the head of somebody still in the house. Once everyone knows where they stand and it is agreed in writing, we can move.

There's still a mortgage on Dad's house. Who is paying it while all this goes on?

The estate is responsible, and interest keeps building until the mortgage is paid off. Ring the lender early and tell them the borrower has died. Many lenders will give the estate some time while probate is dealt with, but that isn't guaranteed, so keep them informed. When the house sells, the mortgage is cleared out of the sale money before anything reaches the beneficiaries. If the debt is bigger than the house is worth, the lender has to agree the sale.

What is this going to cost the estate, and do we pay anything up front?

Nothing up front with us. There are no estate agent fees and no viewings to arrange, and we can cover your legal fees if you use our panel solicitor. You can use your own solicitor instead, which is your right, and the estate would pay that bill. The probate solicitor's charges for the probate work itself are separate. The real cost is the price. We don't publish a percentage, because every property is different and there are too many variables. We price yours on what it is and on what you tell us. We put that in writing the same day. It is our best offer at that point, not an opening number we work up from.

The family just wants this finished. How quickly could it really be done?

Once the Grant is in your hands, completion usually takes 7 to 28 days, and the fastest we have done is 7 days. Before then we can agree the price, get your solicitor instructed and have the paperwork ready, so the day the Grant lands you aren't starting from scratch. We give a written offer the same day and it stands for 14 days. If the family needs longer, we set the date around you.

Would you ever tell us not to sell to you?

Yes, and we do. If the house is in decent order, the beneficiaries aren't in a rush, and the estate isn't losing money every month on bills and insurance, the open market will usually leave more for the family. Our price is lower because we take on the risk and the speed. When that trade isn't worth it for your estate, we will say so plainly.

Do the people inheriting have to agree before I sell?

Legally the decision is yours as executor, not theirs, but bringing them with you is worth the effort. Write down why you chose the route you did, share the valuation, and get beneficiaries to agree in writing where they are willing. That record is what protects you if anyone questions the sale later. Family arguments over a probate house often start with somebody feeling kept in the dark.

Can we sell the house to one of the family for a lower price?

You can, but it needs handling carefully. As executor you still owe a duty to the whole estate, so get an independent valuation first, put your reasons in writing, and get the other beneficiaries to agree in writing too. HMRC can also look closely at a low sale price between family members, so speak to a probate solicitor before fixing a figure. Done properly it is common. Done casually it causes arguments later.

We can't find the EPC or any of the paperwork. Is that a problem?

Missing paperwork doesn't stop us buying. Guarantees, building regulation sign off and old certificates often can't be found for a probate house, and we accept that. An EPC is normally needed when a property is put up for sale, though some exemptions apply, so your solicitor should confirm what your sale needs. Selling direct to us there is no advertising and no viewings, and a missing EPC is something that can be sorted while the sale goes through.

How to verify any cash buyer, including us

There are people in the cash-buying business you wouldn't want to deal with, and a grieving executor is exactly who they look for. The checks that weed them out are quick and free.

Companies House check. Search at find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk. Look for: incorporation date (older = more track record), accounts filed on time, named directors, registered office.

Proof of funds. Ask for a solicitor's letter, on letterhead, dated within 14 days, confirming cleared funds held in client account. Screenshots of a bank balance aren't the same thing and shouldn't satisfy a probate solicitor.

Independent reviews. Google, Trustpilot and any local reviews. Read the detail, not just the star rating. One recent review with real detail beats fifty generic ones.

Redress scheme membership. A reputable buyer is registered with The Property Ombudsman or equivalent. This gives you a complaints route if something goes wrong.

Your right to your own solicitor. You can always use your own. A proper buyer will support that. They won't push you towards one named solicitor as a condition of the offer.

Three independent voices. Citizens Advice, the MoneySavingExpert forum, and any probate solicitor (ideally STEP-qualified) can give you a second opinion. We aren't nervous about you asking them. A buyer who is nervous about that is one to avoid.

Here is what a proper buyer will never do. They won't ask you for a fee up front. They won't ask you for a deposit. They won't push you to sign anything binding before they have put an offer in writing. And they won't insist you use only their solicitor as a condition of the sale.

Ready when you are

We know this is a difficult time. There is no obligation and no hard sell. Tell us about the property when you are ready, and we will put a straightforward cash offer in writing the same day, valid for 14 days. It's our best offer at that point, based on what you have told us, not an opening figure we work up from. It can still change if the legal work turns up something material, such as a title defect or a structural problem. If a cash sale isn't right for your estate, we will say so.

How is the Barnsley property market right now?

The average Barnsley house was worth about £174,000 in early 2026 (HM Land Registry) and prices are edging up. That average won't tell you much about your own house. Barnsley is one of the most split housing markets in England. How your sale goes depends on your postcode and the state of the house, not on the borough average.

How long a house takes to sell here falls into three groups:

Quickest (Penistone, Silkstone, Cawthorne, Dodworth, parts of S74 Elsecar): most sell in about two to three months.

Middle (Wombwell, Hoyland, Mapplewell, Athersley): nearer three to four months.

Slowest (the S72 ex-mining villages: Goldthorpe, Thurnscoe, Grimethorpe, Bolton-upon-Dearne, and parts of S70): four to six months, often longer. More of these are given up on and taken off the market.

Mortgage rates have been coming down, which helps buyers. And a lot of small landlords across S71, S72 and S73 are selling up because of the Renters' Rights Act 2025. There's more on what that Act means for you further down this page.

What this means for you: if your house is in the better parts of Barnsley and in good order, an estate agent usually leaves you with more money, even after fees. A cash sale is worth pricing up if your house sits in a slower postcode, or has PRC, mining or condition problems. Count what it costs you to keep the house while it waits for a buyer. Then do the sums on your own house, not on an average one.

How we price a Barnsley house

We won't put a percentage on your house before we have spoken to you. Barnsley is the cheapest place to buy a house in South Yorkshire, but that average tells us nothing about yours. Too much turns on the details: the postcode, the type of house, the condition, whether there's a tenant in place, whether the title and the mining position are clean, and how quickly you need to be out.

Every property is priced on its own merits and on what you tell us about it. When we come back to you, the figure is our best offer at that point, based on the information provided. We don't open low and then work up to get a deal over the line. The offer goes in writing the same day and stays valid for 14 days.

Conveyancing is the legal work that transfers the house to us. The offer can still change if that work turns up something material, such as a title defect or a structural problem, or if the house turns out to be different from how it was described. Short of that, the number we give you is the number that reaches your account on completion. Nothing comes off it in fees, and we can cover your legal fees if you use our panel solicitor. Typical completion is 7 to 28 days, and the fastest is 7.

Selling in Barnsley by postcode

The market in S70 isn't the market in S75. Here's how selling differs across S70 to S75, plus the S36 and S63 postcodes we also cover.

S70: Barnsley town centre

Victorian and Edwardian terraces, Worsbrough and Stairfoot on the south side, and post-war flats. Roughly £85k to £140k depending on condition. Outside the town centre, houses can sit a long time.

S71. Athersley / Cundy Cross / Monk Bretton

1930s to 1970s semis, mostly family housing. Steady demand. Roughly £140k to £200k, and most sell in about three months.

S72. Goldthorpe / Thurnscoe / Grimethorpe / Bolton-upon-Dearne

Ex-mining and ex-colliery villages. Lots of terraces and ex-council houses, some of them PRC concrete. Roughly £65k to £125k. This is the slowest part of the borough to sell in, and where a cash sale is most often the right answer.

S73. Wombwell / Darfield

Older industrial-era housing mixed with newer estates. Roughly £100k to £180k. A lot of landlords are selling here.

S74. Hoyland / Hoyland Common / Elsecar / Birdwell

Worth more than S73. Elsecar is a heritage village of stone cottages and Victorian housing. Roughly £140k to £260k, with steady demand.

S75. Silkstone / Cawthorne / Dodworth / Mapplewell

The pricier end of the borough. Detached family homes and village properties, from about £260k upwards. These sell fastest.

S36. Penistone

Goldthorpe, Thurnscoe and Bolton-upon-Dearne, overlapping with S72. Older ex-colliery housing, and much the same picture as S72. A cash sale often suits a tired house here.

What are Barnsley's distinctive sale challenges?

Four things make Barnsley houses hard to sell on the open market. In each case the problem is the same. A mortgage lender won't lend on the house without conditions attached, and the buyer walks away rather than deal with them. These are the houses we usually end up buying.

PRC and defective concrete housing

The Housing Defects Act 1984 names types like Airey, Cornish and Wates. Without a PRC repair certificate most lenders won't lend, and agent sales fall through at survey.

Coal mining searches

Almost all of Barnsley sits on old coal workings. Where a search shows shallow workings, common in S72, S73 and parts of S70, lenders often refuse.

Empty-home council tax premium

An empty Barnsley house costs double council tax after 12 months, under the Levelling Up and Regeneration Act 2023. An inherited house can reach that in about two years.

Tenant in situ

You can sell with the tenant in place and skip notice altogether. Since Section 21 ended, that's often the quicker route, and the tenancy transfers with the house.

PRC types found across the borough include Airey, Cornish Unit, Boot, Unity, Wates, Tarran, Orlit, Reema and Parkinson Framed.

How a Barnsley cash sale actually works

The process is short and there's nothing hidden in it.

Step 1. You tell us about the property using the form. Two minutes. Address, type, postcode, brief situation note.

Step 2. We ring you back and ask a few questions. Usually: is there a tenant, has a mining search been done, is there a PRC certificate, is anything outstanding on the title. Then you get a written cash offer the same day.

Step 3. If you accept, our panel solicitors are instructed and we can cover the legal fees. You can use your own solicitor: Sheffield and Barnsley firms (Bury & Walkers Barnsley, Wake Smith, Banner Jones, Switalskis, Irwin Mitchell) all act on Barnsley sales, and we won't press you on this.

Step 4. The legal work takes most of the time. In Barnsley the usual hold-ups are the mining search, tracking down a PRC certificate, and the extra paperwork on a leasehold flat. We chase all of it so you don't have to.

Step 5. Completion in 7 to 28 days, or aligned to a date that suits you: a probate Grant, a divorce settlement, a new property purchase. The pace is yours.

Recent Barnsley developments that affect your sale

Selective licensing started on 15 February 2026. In the designated areas, landlords pay £975 to licence a property. Letting without a licence can cost you up to £30,000. The scheme runs to 14 February 2031.

The Glass Works has brought people back into the town centre, which helps house values in S70.

Goldthorpe compulsory purchase. The council is buying and demolishing 30 houses on Co-op Street and Victoria Street, with new council homes to replace some of them. If you own one, this affects you directly.

New housebuilding is going up on the Barnsley fringes, particularly around Cudworth and Penistone, funded through the South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority.

How to verify any Barnsley cash buyer, including us

The cash-buying industry has people in it whom you wouldn't want to deal with. A short, sensible check filters out the bad actors. None of it takes more than fifteen minutes.

Companies House. Search at find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk.

Proof of funds. A solicitor's letter on letterhead, dated within 14 days, confirming cleared funds in client account. Screenshots of bank balances aren't the same.

Independent reviews. Being honest, we don't have many public reviews yet. The other checks below matter more.

Redress scheme membership. Verify any TPO (The Property Ombudsman) or NAPB (National Association of Property Buyers) claim at tpos.co.uk and napb.co.uk before relying on it.

Your right to your own solicitor. Always available. A legitimate buyer supports this and never pressures you toward only their nominated solicitor.

Three people who don't work for us. Citizens Advice Barnsley (the Dearne, Barnsley and Rotherham service), the SRA register at solicitors.lawsociety.org.uk to check any solicitor, and any local Barnsley conveyancer for a second opinion. None of them has any reason to recommend us.

What a legitimate buyer will never ask for: an upfront fee from you; a deposit from you; a signature on anything binding before they've made you a written offer; an insistence that you use only their solicitor as a condition of the sale.

Frequently asked questions: Barnsley

How fast can you actually buy my Barnsley property?

Completion normally takes 7 to 28 days, and the fastest we have done is 7 days from you accepting the offer. We buy with our own money, so there's no chain, no mortgage application and no broker in the way.

Do you buy "defective" or PRC houses in Barnsley: Airey, Cornish, Boot, Unity?

Yes. We buy the concrete house types listed as defective under Part XVI of the Housing Act 1985, and we don't need a Code 6 repair certificate. An ordinary buyer can't get a mortgage on one of these. We take that risk on instead.

How do you work out your offer?

We don't publish a percentage. Every property is priced on what it actually is and on what you tell us about it, so there is no formula to quote. The figure we give you is our best offer at that point. It goes in writing the same day and stays valid for 14 days. We don't start low and work up to get a deal over the line. It can still change if conveyancing turns up something material, such as a title defect or a structural problem, or if the property turns out to be different from how it was described. For the market-wide picture, see how cash buyer pricing works.

Are there any fees?

No. You pay nothing. Legal fees are covered if you use our panel solicitor; if you use your own solicitor we negotiate that case-by-case, but you never pay us a fee.

Can I use my own solicitor?

Yes, always. Sheffield and Barnsley firms (Bury & Walkers, Wake Smith, Banner Jones, Switalskis, Irwin Mitchell) all act on Barnsley sales. Verify any solicitor at solicitors.lawsociety.org.uk.

What postcodes do you cover in Barnsley?

Every Barnsley postcode, S70 in the town centre through to S75 at Silkstone, Cawthorne and Dodworth. We also cover S36 (Penistone) and S63 (the Dearne villages: Goldthorpe, Thurnscoe and Bolton-upon-Dearne).

What if I'm in mortgage arrears or facing repossession at Barnsley County Court?

We can still help, at any stage, including after a possession order has already been made. Hearings at Barnsley County Court on Westgate are usually listed 6 to 10 weeks ahead, so there is normally time to complete a sale before your date. Our can't afford the mortgage guide sets out your other options too.

What if my property is tenanted? Do I need to evict first under the Renters' Rights Act 2025?

No. We buy with the tenant in situ, common for buy-to-let exits under the Act. You avoid the four-month Ground 1A notice and the 12-month re-let ban entirely. The new owner takes the tenancy across as part of the purchase.

What about Barnsley's selective licensing scheme?

Barnsley's scheme started on 15 February 2026 and runs to 14 February 2031. In the designated areas it costs £975 to licence a property, and letting without a licence can cost you up to £30,000. Selling to a cash buyer is a clean way out of it.

How do I know you're a legitimate buyer, not a scam?

Six quick checks. Look the company up at Companies House and check the buyer’s registration. Ask for proof of funds in a solicitor's letter. Check any solicitor on the SRA register. Look for independent reviews. Remember you can always use your own solicitor. And get a second opinion from Citizens Advice. We explain each of these above.

What if I change my mind?

Before exchange of contracts you can walk away at no cost. Heads of terms are non-binding under section 2 of the Law of Property (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1989. After exchange both parties are legally bound. That is the pivot point, we explain it before any signature.

Frequently asked questions

Do you buy properties on old mining ground in S72?

Yes. Almost the entire borough sits in a Coal Mining Reporting Area. CON29M shallow-workings flags don't block a cash purchase, they block mortgaged ones.

Who actually buys houses for cash around Barnsley, and are you local or national?

We are a local cash buyer, not a national call centre passing your details on. We buy directly with our own funds. We work across Barnsley week in, week out. Our team and investor clients have bought 100+ properties between them, so we price a Grimethorpe terrace and a Penistone cottage very differently.

It's been on with an agent for months and nothing's happening. What do I do now?

First, ask your agent for the honest numbers: how many viewings, how many second viewings, how many offers. If the answer is very few, the price or the condition is usually the problem, not the marketing. You can drop the price, spend money on the work, try an auction, or sell to us for cash. We will tell you straight which of those we think suits your house.

My house is in a right state. Will you still want it?

Yes. We buy in any condition and we actually prefer houses that need work. Damp, an old roof, dodgy wiring, a garden like a jungle, a house full of furniture nobody has cleared: none of it puts us off. You don't need to tidy, decorate, clear it out or get quotes for repairs. The condition is already priced into what we offer you.

Do I have to have loads of strangers traipsing round my house?

No. There are no open days, no evening viewings and no strangers being shown round. We come once for a short look, either in person or on a video call, and that is it. There is no For Sale board outside and no listing on Rightmove or Zoopla. After that visit we put the offer in writing the same day.

Will the neighbours find out I'm selling? I'd rather keep it quiet.

Mostly you can keep it quiet. With no board outside and no online listing, most neighbours won't know until the sale is done. We can't promise complete secrecy though, and nobody honestly can. Once the sale completes, the price is recorded at the Land Registry like every other sale in England and Wales, and anyone can look it up later.

I need the money by a certain date. Can you work to that?

Yes. Tell us the date you need and we will work back from it. Completion normally takes 7 to 28 days, and the fastest we have done is 7 days, but we can also go slower and aim for a date that suits you, such as the day a probate grant comes through, a court settlement date, or the day you get the keys to your next place. If your date looks too tight, we will say so rather than promise it.

Mum's house in Goldthorpe has sat empty since she passed. Can you take it off our hands?

Yes, though you will usually need the grant of probate before the sale can complete. We can agree the price and get the legal side lined up while you wait for it, so completion follows soon after the grant lands. That matters in Barnsley because an empty house starts costing more in council tax once it has been empty a year, on top of the insurance and standing charges.

If I ask what you'd pay, am I signing up to anything?

No. Asking what we would pay doesn't tie you to anything. We put the offer in writing the same day, it stays open for 14 days, and you are free to sit on it, show it to family, get an estate agent valuation to compare, or say no and never hear from us again.

Would I be better off just sticking with an estate agent?

We assess each property individually, taking account of its condition, location, tenure and the information you share. We explain our offer and its conditions in writing. There is no obligation to accept, and you can ask your solicitor to review the terms.

What's to stop you knocking the price down at the last minute once I'm too far in to back out?

Our written offer is valid for 14 days, based on what you have told us and what we see. We don't agree a price and then chip away at it near the end to squeeze you. The one thing that can change a price is something serious turning up in the legal checks, such as a title problem or a structural issue nobody knew about. If that happens we explain it and you can walk away.

Do you only buy houses, or would you take a flat or an ex-council place?

Both, plus most other things. We buy terraces, semis, detached houses, bungalows, flats, ex-council and old coal board housing right across the borough. Empty, part-built, fire damaged or boarded up is all fine, and tenanted sales are covered separately on this page. Leasehold flats take a little longer because of the paperwork from the freeholder. If we aren't the right buyer for it, we will tell you rather than string you along.

How do I get started without ending up on a list getting rung every day?

Fill in the short form on this page or ring 07445 629113, and give us the address plus a sentence about your situation. We ring you back as fast as we can. You deal with the same small team the whole way through, and you won't be passed around a call centre. If you tell us the answer is no, that is the end of it.

How is the Chesterfield property market right now?

Prices are steady and a little higher than a year ago. The average Chesterfield home was worth £188,400 in February 2026 (HM Land Registry). That is a bit more than Barnsley and a good deal less than Sheffield, which is what you would expect of a town that acts as a Sheffield satellite.

How long a sale takes depends on where in Chesterfield you are:

Quickest: S42 Wingerworth, Holymoorside and Ashover. Usually a couple of months.

Steady: S40 Brampton and Walton. Around three months.

Slower: S41 Whittington and S43 Brimington. Often four or five months.

Slowest: the ex-coalfield streets in S43 Staveley and Inkersall, S44 Bolsover and older parts of S45 Clay Cross. Half a year is common, and about one seller in five gives up and takes the house off the market.

The bigger picture is steady but not easy. The Bank of England has cut rates three times from their peak, but borrowing is still dear and buyers are cautious. The Renters' Rights Act 2025 came into force on 1 May 2026. It scrapped Section 21 and replaced it with a Ground 1A notice: four months' notice, plus a ban on re-letting for 12 months if you decide to keep the property after all. A lot of small landlords in S41, S43, S44 and S45 are deciding to get out.

Chesterfield has Sheffield postcodes but Derbyshire councils. That matters when you sell. Chesterfield Borough Council covers S40, S41 and parts of S42 and S43. North East Derbyshire DC covers S45 and parts of S42. Bolsover DC covers S44 and parts of S43. Your council tax, the empty-homes premium, planning rules and your local court (Chesterfield Justice Centre, S41 7TD) are all Derbyshire. National cash-buying sites miss this, and several map the postcodes wrongly.

What would we offer for a Chesterfield house?

We don't work to a percentage. Two houses on the same street can be worth very different money once you allow for condition, tenure, mining history and flood risk. Every postcode from S40 to S45 has its own pattern too. So we price the house in front of us, on what it is and what you tell us, rather than running it through a formula.

Selling in Chesterfield by postcode

S40 isn't the same market as S45. National sites treat Chesterfield as one place. It isn't. Here is how the postcodes differ, with the council that sends your bill.

S40: Town centre / Brampton / Walton

Victorian and Edwardian terraces, 1930s semis, post-war estates. Includes the Crooked Spire conservation area. £125k-£320k. Brampton (S40 4) is the borough's strongest middle-class postcode. Chesterfield BC bills.

S41: Whittington / Sheepbridge / Newbold

Working-class former-industrial neighbourhoods, ex-NCB terraces, 1960s semis, ex-council stock. £105k-£235k. Longest days-on-market in the town. Chesterfield BC bills.

S42: Wingerworth / Holymoorside / Ashover

Stone cottages, detached executive, village vernacular. Peak District fringe. £180k-£550k. Strongest demand, fastest sales. NE Derbyshire DC bills.

S43: Brimington / Staveley / Inkersall / Mastin Moor

Ex-coalfield terraces, 1950s ex-council, new build on the Staveley regeneration sites. £110k-£195k. Staveley Town Deal work under way. Mining search flags are routine here. Chesterfield BC bills (Bolsover DC for parts).

S44. Bolsover / Clowne / Calow / Shuttlewood

Ex-NCB terraces, ex-council semis. £95k-£185k, lowest in the borough footprint. Bolsover Castle, Markham Vale (M1 J29A). Bolsover DC bills.

S45: Clay Cross / Ashover / North Wingfield / Pilsley

Ex-mining terraces, 1980s estates, stone cottages, Avant/Persimmon new build at The Avenue. £120k-£260k. Clay Cross Town Deal work under way. NE Derbyshire DC bills.

We also buy in immediately adjacent postcodes: S18 (Dronfield), S21 (Killamarsh/Eckington), DE55 / DE56 in the south, NG20 (Shirebrook). If your property is on the Chesterfield ring of villages, ask us.

What are Chesterfield's distinctive sale challenges?

Some Chesterfield houses are far harder to sell through an agent than the market figures suggest. Usually it's because a lender won't touch them, and buyers give up rather than fight it. There are four reasons we see again and again.

North Derbyshire Coalfield

Almost every house in Chesterfield sits over old coal workings, and that scares off buyers who need a mortgage. The whole borough is inside the Coal Mining Reporting Area.

HS2 cancellation and Staveley

Cancelling HS2 didn't wipe out Chesterfield prices, whatever a buyer tells you. The eastern leg went in October 2023, but the gain had never really been priced in.

Empty-home premium, three councils

Leave a house empty a year and your council tax doubles. All three councils charge 100% after 12 months, rising to 200% after 5 years and 300% after 10.

Selling with a tenant

You can sell with the tenant still living there and skip the notice period. Since Section 21 went, Ground 1A means four months' notice and a re-let ban.

Collieries at Markham Colliery, Bolsover, Bolsover, Glapwell, Arkwright, Renishaw Park, Ireland, Williamthorpe and Holmewood all worked this ground. The Staveley regeneration and the Station Quarter carried on after HS2. The empty-home premium sits under the Levelling-up and Regeneration Act 2023, covering S40, S41, S43 and parts of S42. Mining subsidence sits under the Coal Mining Subsidence Act 1991.
